name: Katie Dunwell

bio.statement: A City of Wilsonville notice dated September 22, 2025 says Dunwell informed the city manager she was resigning from the City Council effective immediately.
bio.excerpt: Katie Dunwell has informed City Manager Bryan Cosgrove that she is resigning from the Council, effective immediately.

source.publisher: City of Wilsonville, 'Katie Dunwell Resigns from City Council'

bio.statement: Dunwell's pamphlet statement lists her as a retired digital strategist, formerly a marketing vice president and investment banking partner.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Digital Strategist, Retired Occupational Background: Vice President of Marketing; Partner, Investment Banking

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists Wilsonville City Council and the Development Review Board as prior governmental experience, and a B.A. from Portland State University.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: B.A., Portland State University Prior Governmental Experience: Wilsonville City Council, Development Review Board

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Dunwell says she will push for transparency before spending decisions are made rather than after.
positions.excerpt: I will push for transparency before spending decisions are made, not after

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Dunwell says she supports a vibrant Town Center but wants an honest feasibility review before tax dollars are committed.
positions.excerpt: I support a vibrant Town Center, but residents deserve an honest feasibility review before we commit tax dollars.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Dunwell says she will fight to include affordable starter homes in Wilsonville's housing mix.
positions.excerpt: I’ll fight to include affordable starter homes in the mix, because owning a home remains the greatest path to generational wealth.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Dunwell says she will advocate for streamlined permitting and treat businesses as partners.
positions.excerpt: I’ll advocate for streamlined permitting and treat businesses as partners, not adversaries.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: In a joint pamphlet argument with Jennie Hill on Measure 3-641, Dunwell says they are voting no on the Town Center urban renewal financing plan.
positions.excerpt: We are voting no on the Town Center urban renewal financing plan.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 79, printed C-78)
